notes: The African American Citywide Historic Context Statement, adopted 21 February 2024. A citywide cultural statement with no appendix inventory and no APNs: its address-level material is in the narrative, in the per-chapter 'Remaining Properties' and 'Commemorative Sites' lists, and in two lists at the back - the properties recommended for landmark or register designation, and the candidates for historic plaques. Its two appendices, which are the only tables in the document, list people and organisations without addresses. A large share of what it names is non-extant: the statement says so itself, since the 1906 fire took the nineteenth-century enclave next to Chinatown and the Redevelopment Agency took most of what the Fillmore had built since.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in this document. Its subject overlaps the LGBTQ+ statements (issues #63, #64, #65) on the Tenderloin and Fillmore addresses, and the New Deal statement (already read) on Aquatic Park and the Westside Courts.
coverage.note: Every page of the PDF was scanned for numbered addresses by two passes - one for named streets, one for the ordinal-numbered streets (3rd, 9th, 10th, 16th, 18th, 28th) the first pass cannot see - and every matching passage was read in context. Sites the statement names only by intersection, park, street or military post are not here: the Buffalo Soldiers' barracks at the Presidio, the Bayview Neighborhood Center at Third and Mendell, St. Cyprian A.M.E. at Jackson and St. James, the 'Colored Colony' bounded by Stockton, Kearny, Washington and Broadway, Bell Mews at Divisadero and Ellis, Garnett Terrace at Hudson and Whitney Young, George Washington High School at 33rd and Geary, the murals listed only by intersection, and Hunters Point Naval Shipyard.
